title: Acute Respiratory Failure: Oxygenation Strategies and Escalation of Care
summary: Evidence-based approach to initial oxygen therapy, noninvasive strategies (HFNO, CPAP/NIV), and timely intubation with lung-protective ventilation for acute hypoxemic or hypercapnic respiratory failure. Emphasis on individualized targets, dynamic reassessment, and avoidance of delayed intubation.
clinicalQuestion: What are the optimal oxygenation strategies and escalation steps for adults with acute respiratory failure in the ICU and ED?

heroStats.label: Lung-protective ventilation
heroStats.value: VT 6 mL/kg PBW, low plateau pressure [8], [9]

keyMoments.title: Define the phenotype early
keyMoments.body: Differentiate hypoxemic vs hypercapnic failure; identify ARDS, COPD exacerbation, cardiogenic pulmonary edema, or immunocompromised host to tailor oxygenation strategy and escalation [7], [1], [2].

keyMoments.title: Start with safe oxygen targets
keyMoments.body: Initiate O2 for SpO2 <90–92% or PaO2 <60 mm Hg; aim for SpO2 92–96% (88–92% if chronic hypercapnia risk) to avoid hypoxemia and hyperoxia-related harm [1], [2].

keyMoments.title: Prefer HFNO for AHRF
keyMoments.body: HFNO provides heated, humidified high FiO2 with flow-related PEEP, reduces work of breathing, and lowers intubation compared with standard oxygen in many AHRF settings [3], [4], [1], [2].

keyMoments.title: Use NIV where evidence is strongest
keyMoments.body: NIV/CPAP is highly effective in acute hypercapnic COPD and cardiogenic pulmonary edema; monitor closely for failure to prevent harmful delays in intubation [5], [6], [7].

keyMoments.title: Intubate when criteria met
keyMoments.body: Failing noninvasive support, altered mental status, refractory hypoxemia, shock, or inability to protect airway warrant prompt intubation and lung-protective ventilation [7], [8], [9].

sections.title: Stabilize, Classify, and Set Oxygen Targets
sections.blurb: Rapid ABCs, phenotype-based strategy, and tight oxygen titration.

steps.title: Assess severity and phenotype
steps.body: Identify hypoxemic AHRF (e.g., pneumonia/ARDS), hypercapnic failure (COPD/asthma), or mixed etiologies. Obtain SpO2, ABG/VBG, RR, work of breathing, mental status, hemodynamics, and chest imaging [7], [1], [2].

steps.title: Set oxygenation targets
steps.body: Aim SpO2 92–96% for most; in suspected chronic hypercapnia (COPD/OSA/obesity hypoventilation), target 88–92% to avoid oxygen-induced hypercapnia [1], [2].

steps.title: Start oxygen safely
steps.body: Begin with nasal cannula or nonrebreather as needed while preparing definitive support. Avoid prolonged FiO2 1.0; titrate to target and reassess within minutes [1], [2].

sections.title: High-Flow Nasal Oxygen (HFNO) as First-Line for AHRF
sections.blurb: HFNO is increasingly the reference therapy for AHRF with benefits on intubation risk.

steps.title: Initiation
steps.body: Start flow 40–60 L/min, FiO2 to achieve target SpO2; increase flow for dyspnea and to reduce entrainment. Use heated humidification to improve tolerance [3], [4], [1], [2].

steps.title: Physiology and benefits
steps.body: HFNO provides high FiO2, low-level PEEP, dead-space washout, and reduced work of breathing. Evidence suggests **reduced intubation risk** vs standard oxygen in AHRF (moderate certainty) [3], [4], [1], [2].

steps.title: Monitoring and time-limited trial
steps.body: Reassess at 30–60 minutes: respiratory rate, SpO2/FiO2, ROX index, mental status. **Escalate if ROX remains low or work of breathing is high** to avoid delayed intubation [1], [2].

sections.title: CPAP/NIV: When and How
sections.blurb: Use where evidence is strongest; avoid prolonged ineffective trials.

steps.title: COPD exacerbation with hypercapnic acidosis
steps.body: NIV is first-line; meta-analytic data show **reduced intubation and mortality** vs standard therapy [5], [6], [7]. Start IPAP/EPAP tailored to pH, PaCO2, and work of breathing; aim to correct acidosis and reduce RR.

steps.title: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema
steps.body: CPAP/NIV rapidly improves oxygenation and dyspnea; reduces need for intubation in many studies. Ensure hemodynamic optimization in parallel [7].

steps.title: Hypoxemic AHRF (non-COPD)
steps.body: Evidence is mixed; HFNO is generally preferred. Select NIV for selected patients with high work of breathing and close monitoring. Consider helmet interface where available; trials show variable results vs HFNO in COVID-19 AHRF [10], [1], [2].

steps.title: Operational safety
steps.body: Use tight-fitting interface, early ABG reassessment (30–60 min), and predefined failure criteria. **Do not persist with NIV in worsening hypoxemia, acidosis, or encephalopathy** [5], [7], [1], [2].

sections.title: Intubation and Lung-Protective Ventilation
sections.blurb: Recognize failure early and apply lung-protective strategies.

steps.title: Indications for intubation
steps.body: Refractory hypoxemia (e.g., SpO2 <90% with high FiO2), persistent/worsening acidosis or hypercapnia despite NIV, inability to protect airway, severe work of breathing, shock, or altered mental status [7], [1], [2].

steps.title: Initial ventilator settings
steps.body: Use **VT 6 mL/kg PBW**, limit plateau pressure, adjust PEEP/FiO2 per ARDS principles, and target adequate oxygenation without hyperoxia [8], [9].

steps.title: Adjuncts and rescue
steps.body: For severe ARDS: higher PEEP strategy, early prone positioning, conservative fluids; consider neuromuscular blockade and extracorporeal support in refractory cases per local expertise [8], [9].

sections.title: Practical Targets, Failure Signs, and Pearls
sections.blurb: Use this grid during bedside reassessment.

cards.title: Failure signs (escalate)
items: Persistent tachypnea, escalating FiO2 on HFNO/NIV [1], [2]
Worsening acidosis or rising PaCO2 on NIV [5], [6], [7]
Inability to clear secretions or protect airway [7]

cards.title: Reassessment cadence
items: HFNO/NIV: check at 30–60 minutes after initiation and after each change [1], [2]
ABG/VBG after starting NIV or if clinical status changes [7]
Continuous pulse oximetry; avoid sustained SpO2 >96% [1], [2]

cards.title: Safety pearls
items: Humidification and adequate flow on HFNO to reduce dyspnea/work of breathing [3], [4], [1]
Predefine intubation criteria to avoid delays [7], [1], [2]
Use lung-protective ventilation from the first breath post-intubation [8], [9]

cards.title: COVID-19 specific notes
items: HFNO is safe with precautions; alternating with NIV/helmet may help select patients [10]
Trial data show variable effects on mortality/intubation; individualize and monitor closely [10]

cards.title: Pathophysiology anchors
items: HFNO: high FiO2, low PEEP, dead-space washout [3], [4], [1]
NIV: improves alveolar ventilation (↓ PaCO2), unloads respiratory muscles [5], [6], [7]
